tax.heading: Income Taxes
tax.text: Income taxes are provided based on the liability method of accounting. The provision for income taxes is based on pretax financial income. Deferred tax assets and liabilities are recognized for the future expected tax consequences of temporary differences between income tax and financial reporting and principally relate to differences in the tax basis of assets and liabilities and their reported amounts, using enacted tax rates in effect for the year in which differences are expected to reverse.

net.heading: Net Income per Share
net.text:
Basic earnings per share (“EPS”) are computed by dividing net earnings by the weighted average number of common shares outstanding for the period.

Diluted EPS attributable to common shareholders is computed by adjusting net earnings by the weighted average number of common shares and potential common shares outstanding (if dilutive) during each period. Potential common shares include shares of restricted stock units as if the units issued by us were vested and convertible debt. We apply the treasury stock method to account for the dilutive impact of its restricted stock units and the if converted method for its convertible notes. Anti-dilutive securities are excluded from diluted EPS. As a result of determining the effect of potentially dilutive securities, in certain periods, diluted net loss per share is the same as the basic net loss per share for the periods presented.

da.text: The reserve estimates are used in the depreciation, depletion and amortization calculations and our internal cash flow projections. The reserve estimates are prepared by professional engineers, both internal and external, and are subject to change over time as more data becomes available. sbc.heading: Stock-based Compensation
sbc.text: Stock-based compensation for restricted stock units is measured at the grant date based on the fair value of the award and is recognized as expense over the applicable vesting period of the stock award (generally two to four years ) using the straight-line method.

wc.heading: Accounts Receivable
wc.text: The timing of revenue recognition, billings and cash collections results in accounts receivable from customers. Customers are invoiced as power is delivered or as coal is shipped or at periodic intervals in accordance with contractual terms. Coal invoices typically include customary adjustments for the resolution of price variability, such as coal quality thresholds. Payments are generally received within thirty days of invoicing. Historically, credit losses have been insignificant. No charges for credit losses were recognized during the years ended December 31, 2024 or 2023.

intro.text: Hallador Energy Company (“Hallador” or the “Company”) is a vertically integrated, independent power producer (“IPP”) and fuel company with operations primarily in Indiana. The Company operates across multiple stages of the energy value chain, from accredited capacity and energy to coal. The Company’s electric operations are located within the Midcontinent Independent System Operator’s ("MISO") footprint. Our operations comprise Hallador Power Company, LLC (“Hallador Power”) that provides accredited capacity and energy to utilities and other energy market participants through its MISO interconnection, and Sunrise Coal, LLC (“Sunrise”) that mines bituminous coal in Indiana to serve various power plants in the Midwest and Southeast United States.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Equity-method investments
lines.why: Stakes in associated businesses, usually part of operations. Financial if held as an investment.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Current portion of long-term debt
lines.why: Borrowed money falling due within a year: financial.

lines.name: Finance lease liabilities
lines.why: Leases that work like a loan for the asset: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue, non-current
lines.why: Customers' payments for later years: operating.

lines.name: Other assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total assets minus the lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total liabilities minus the lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

s.t: Segment operating revenues from electric operations increased $49.2 million, or 18.8%, compared to 2024 attributable to an increase in sales of delivered energy while accredited capacity revenue was stable.
Although we have many long, well-established relationships with our key suppliers, we do not believe that we are dependent on any of our individual suppliers other than for purchases of electricity.
Purchases of certain underground mining equipment are concentrated with one principal supplier; however, supplier competition continues to develop.

We depend on a limited number of customers for a significant portion of our revenues, and the loss of one or more significant customers could affect our ability to maintain the sales volume, price of our products and profitability.
Our ability to receive payment for electric power, accredited capacity and coal sold and delivered depends on the continued creditworthiness of our customers.
These prices depend upon factors beyond our control, including:
Estimates of coal reserves necessarily depend upon a number of variables and assumptions, any one of which could vary considerably from actual results.
We rely on information technology to operate our business.
Water is supplied by public water services, surface impoundments, or water wells.
Approximately 47.0% of the 2025 net hourly purchases occurred in the fourth quarter as a result of the equipment issues.
Although we actively monitor the creditworthiness of our key vendors, the financial failure of a key vendor could disrupt our operations and have an adverse impact on our revenue and cash flows.
